name: Timphan
note: A steamed Acehnese sweet wrapped in banana leaves.

name: Tari Barong
note: Barong and Rangda dramatize the struggle between good and evil in Balinese performance.

name: Tari Campak
note: This lively Bangka Belitung dance entertains guests at weddings and other gatherings.

name: Musik Dol
note: Dol drums accompany Bengkulu’s Tabot observance and other cultural performances.

name: Seba Baduy
note: Baduy representatives bring harvest offerings during a customary visit to regional leaders.

name: Tumbilotohe
note: Lamps illuminate Gorontalo homes and streets during the final nights of Ramadan.

name: Tari Selampit Delapan
note: Eight dancers weave coloured scarves or cords through coordinated movement.

name: Udeng Ponorogo
note: In Ponorogo, different folded headcloth styles relate to social roles and ritual use.

name: Gambang kromong
note: A Betawi ensemble combining Chinese and local musical traditions.

name: Bubur pedas Sambas
note: Roasted rice, vegetables and herbs make a fragrant Sambas Malay porridge.

name: Baju adat Takwo
note: This Kutai formal outfit features dark fabric and golden decoration around the collar and sleeves.

name: Teluk belanga
note: This traditional Malay men’s outfit is documented in Lingga’s dress traditions.

name: Bagajah gamuling baular lulut
note: In this Banjar wedding style, the bride wears an udat chest wrap with jasmine adornments.

name: Baju Pawang
note: Kaharingan ritual specialists wear this wood-fibre garment with fringe and beads when offering prayers.

name: Busana perempuan Ta’a
note: Kenyah women wear ta’a attire with colourful beadwork, a tradition shared with East Kalimantan.

name: Mahkota siger
note: Women wear this golden-colored crown as part of Lampung ceremonial dress.

name: Baju cele
note: Maluku’s cele shirt is known for small checks or geometric stripes.

name: Busana keraton Manteren Lamo
note: A red closed jacket with silver buttons marks this sultanate dress tradition.

name: Lambung Sasak
note: Sasak women in Lombok wear this black sleeveless top with a long cloth at customary ceremonies.

name: Ti’i langga Rote
note: This distinctive hat made from dried lontar palm leaves is part of Rote men’s customary dress.

name: Manik-manik Sentani
note: Mori-mori beads are among the adornments worn by Isosolo dancers around Lake Sentani.

name: Lukisan kulit kayu khombow
note: Artists in Asei Besar paint bark with motifs rooted in Sentani nature and local knowledge.

name: Kerajinan monga Arfak
note: Women in Manokwari make Arfak noken using mincauw bark fibre and pineapple-leaf fibre.

name: Baju kurung Melayu
note: This loose-fitting garment is part of Malay dress traditions in Riau.

name: Randai Kuantan
note: This Kuantan Singingi theater uses dialogue, sung pantun, and instrumental accompaniment.

name: Kabasaran
note: This Minahasan warrior dance is performed in striking ceremonial costume.

name: Saluang
note: The saluang is a bamboo flute used in Minangkabau music.

name: Tari Linda
note: A Muna dance associated with the Karia customary ceremony.

name: Tari Pa'gellu
note: A Toraja dance performed on joyful occasions.

name: Tari Pattuqduq Towaine
note: A Mandar welcoming dance performed by women.

name: Tari Gending Sriwijaya
note: This Palembang welcome dance evokes the grandeur of the former Srivijaya kingdom.

name: Tari Dero
note: This communal dance from Poso expresses joy and togetherness in Pamona communities.

name: Tortor
note: Tortor dancing is an important part of Batak customary ceremonies.
